$comment: The events module's register. events/tools/fetch.py reads this file; events/AGENTS.md explains the fields. An id here is the `source` value on every event the calendar contributes, and the prefix of that event's `id`.

sources.name: Illuminate
sources.note: The City of Awe's free-concert calendar. One iCal feed carries the upcoming slate but no per-event URL; each event is a WordPress `se-event` post, so `links` (the REST API, newest first) supplies its page, matched on start time and title. An event the API doesn't return links the public `page`. LOCATION is a street address with no venue name, so venues.json does the naming. robots.txt disallows nothing relevant.

sources.name: SF Rec & Park
sources.note:
CivicPlus. Each calendar in the issue's CID list has its own iCalendar feed at common/modules/iCalendar/iCalendar.aspx?catID=&feed=calendar; several are empty by design. LOCATION is 'Venue - address' text, occasionally wrapped in

tags. robots.txt disallows /RSS.aspx and /map.aspx but not calendar.aspx or the iCalendar feed.

sources.name: Nature in the City
sources.note: Squarespace events collection; ?format=json lists `upcoming` with title, startDate/endDate (ms epoch) and a location object whose mapLat/mapLng are real when set and the Squarespace default (40.7207559, -74.0007613) when not. The /calendar page is an empty shell — the collection is /events.

sources.name: Alemany Farm
sources.note: No feed: the workshops page is hand-maintained WordPress markup — each workshop is an <h3>, a <strong> line with the date and hours, and an Eventbrite register button. All events are at the farm. robots.txt allows everything but asks Crawl-Delay: 20 — one request per run.

sources.name: Friends of Sunset Dunes
sources.note: Squarespace events collection like natureinthecity's. Same NYC-default coordinate sentinel to drop. Venues are usually entrances along the park ('Sunset Dunes @ Irving'); the addressTitle names the spot.

sources.name: SF Rec & Park special event permits
sources.note: The Permits & Reservations office's tentative calendars of special events: the page links the year's special-event master spreadsheet as PDFs, one per area and one with every area ('<year> RPD Special Event Master ALL'). The files are replaced (new DocumentCenter ids) as the year fills in, so fetch.py reads the page for the current link on every run, and a new year's file is picked up the day it is linked — that is how this page is re-checked for updates. One row per permit, site and day; only rows whose status is P or I are approved, and rows carry dates but no times, so every event is all-day and gives way to a timed listing of the same event on the venue's own calendar. robots.txt disallows neither the page nor /DocumentCenter.

sources.name: Yerba Buena Gardens Festival
sources.note: Free outdoor performing arts, mostly in Yerba Buena Gardens, roughly May to October; out of season the list is empty and shows only 'latest past' programs, which resolve() drops. WordPress with The Events Calendar. robots.txt disallows every URL with a query string (`Disallow: /*?`), which rules out the iCal export (?ical=1) and the REST API's paging (?page=N), and asks Crawl-delay: 3. So fetch.py reads the HTML list view and follows its path-based next link (/events/list/page/N/), 3 seconds apart. Each event names its venue as 'Great Lawn, Yerba Buena Gardens' plus a street line; venues.json does the matching. Checked 2026-11-21.
